look_here_first: ROUGH DROPSEED (*Sporobolus clandestinus*): find a perennial fine-leaved tuft, then the long narrow tightly CONTRACTED but BRANCHED PANICLE; Bob Harms SPCL-a1 (field tufts), SPCL-I/i1 (green to mature narrow panicle) and SPCL-b (same above-ground upper culm with partly sheathed blooming head) show real source species, not Hays specimen proof. Learn genuinely EXSERTED PURPLE ANTHERS in J/J1/J2, then isolate ONE single-FLORETED AWNLESS spikelet in source SPCL-S, showing small outer glumes, inner lemma/palea and detached pale actual grains; treat tiny subparts cautiously until precise arrow QA. The real blade/sheath junction SPCL-L is a source-scale reference to ~0.2–0.3mm ligule HAIR FRINGE (NOT large membrane). Most decisive versus composite: a properly mature SAME-PLANT dry/wet grain shows pericarp loosening WITHOUT becoming gelatinous and slipping off, plus abundant prickle cells on actual abaxial lemma at 400×. Bob Harms published genuine documented wet-grain and compound-scope evidence in separately copyrighted research (study source links), not incorrectly CC-labelled panel media. S. vaginiflorus has short-lived annual root system and sheath flowers but field habit overlaps; retain original native county approval/holds.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — Purola Preserve natural flora; Travis and Williamson — county distribution layer explicitly records both counties.

best_field_traits: ligule a very short fringe of hairs
crew_field_check: Perennial dropseed with a tight, slender panicle; can closely resemble composite dropseed. Narrowness is a field clue, not proof. True discriminators include glume-to-lemma proportions and mature grain pericarp (typically NOT gelatinizing/slipping off the seed when freshly wetted); lemma prickle features need a compound microscope for confident scoring.
1-flowered, awnless Sporobolus spikelets — not the multi-flowered bristled clusters of Setaria/Cenchrus.
Photographs of head outline are first clues, NOT confirmed lemma/pericarp identification.
Anther/flower color, panicle width and small/large height alone are not safe identifications.
photo_diagnostic_second_pass_20261022: 1. Look at SPCL-a1 regional live stiff culm tuft. Two currently stored real Cleveland Powell photos give extra panicle context; find and photograph a rooted base before calling it a persistent perennial crown. Field scenery cannot prove local identity.
2. In SPCL-b see the actual terminal flowering head partly emerging from an upper sheath. That original three-view plate is an UPPER CULM and sheath, NOT a complete rooted whole plant.

3. Follow the contracted main axis through SPCL-I (green developing short-branch head) and i1 (mature straw tan densely arranged narrow head). It looks spike-like but has lateral branching, so call it a tight PANICLE, not an Elymus-like true spike.

4. In SPCL-I2, J, J1, J2 examine genuine dark exserted ANTHERS on filament-like stalks between green-purple spear-shaped bracts. They are pollen-bearing organs, NOT lemma awns; Sporobolus florets are awnless.

5. One detached sample in SPCL-S shows a real ONE-FLORETED SPIKELET. Locate the two narrow outer GLUMES below one fertile inner lemma/palea. The pale grain shown separately is not an intact spikelet. No new fine arrow until exact glume and palea pixels cross-verified.

6. SPCL-L shows an exact source blade/sheath junction. Real ligule is very SHORT HAIR FRINGE ~0.2–0.3 mm, not a large membranous flap or the broad ragged sheath tissue. Individual hair-tip pinpoint/measurement pending true 20–40× picture.

7. Wet-test study (LINK ONLY, NOT duplicated photograph): on Harms separately documented SPORO comparison the dry S. clandestinus grains vs 20/36-min water microscope shots show PERICARP LOOSENING but still hugging the seed, compared with compositus grains tending to swell/jelly and SLIP. This is not a universal binary test, especially on old/varying collections.

8. True MICROSCOPIC clue (STUDY LINK ONLY): Harms Cscope-lemma research photographed rough-dropseed abundant PRICKLES and silica cells at 100× and 400× versus composite-dropseed larger silica cells and fewer prickle fields and poverty-dropseed hooks. These structures are NOT resolved in any of the new regular phone/photo panels.

9. Compare *S. compositus* actual mature spikelets/seed response and perennial varieties; SPCL narrow spike-like head alone is not diagnostic. Compare *S. vaginiflorus* small seasonal rooted plant and upper-sheath florals; some hidden flowers overlap.

10. Collect and photograph source-identified same living Hays rooted flowering specimen, true glume and lemma at 1mm scale, actual hair ligule microscope and same source mature grain wet test 0/2/5/10/20/40 minutes, and inspect original four source arrows on phone. If missing, hold `FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS`.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Gather mature grains and intact glume/lemma, not just plant silhouette.
field_matrix.difference: Both perennial; S. compositus pericarp typically gelatinizes and separates when wetted, unlike S. clandestinus. Panicle form overlaps and varieties complicate appearance.
field_matrix.guardrail: Fresh mature seed is needed: older stored seed may react slowly or poorly; use multiple characters.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Check basal roots and crown, panicle and concealed upper-sheath spikelets.
field_matrix.difference: Typically a much shorter annual with terminal and axillary panicles; annual versus perennial is helpful on a rooted adult, not always clear in a drought-stunted plant.
field_matrix.guardrail: Concealed sheath spikelets are not exclusive to poverty dropseed in this section.

not_reliable_alone: Presence of hidden sheath flowers (multiple related dropseeds can have these)
Being taller/shorter or open/contracted at a single drought-stressed moment
Claiming a micro-lemma character from an ordinary phone photograph

Local same-plant source and true measured tiny ligule, detached glumes/lemma, and 400× verified confirmation remain holds.

visual_comparison.title: Rough dropseed — real Central Texas flowering, true spikelet/grain dissection and leaf collar
visual_comparison.subtitle: Eleven individual source-photographed © Bob Harms exact rough dropseed field/anatomy panels alongside two stored CC BY plant views and two previously recorded other-species comparisons. Ripe grain wet-test research evidence is linked but NOT copied without specific rights. Eleven original Harms photos now physically stored in GitHub, retaining attribution and restricted educational rights.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: ROUGH DROPSEED: PERENNIAL fine leafy tuft → long very NARROW contracted PANICLE → ONE-FLORETED, AWNLESS spikelets (ca. 5–7mm in GrassBase) → 2 BASAL glumes enclosing pubescent lemma/palea and exposed ~2–3mm grain. Truly short 0.2–0.3mm HAIR LIGULE. Fresh grain pericarp loosens but does NOT jelly/slip off like composite; lemma PRICKLES require 400×.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Rough dropseed — flowering anthers, one-floret spikelet, actual seeds and pericarp comparison
steps: 1. Look at SPCL-a1 regional live stiff culm tuft. Two currently stored real Cleveland Powell photos give extra panicle context; find and photograph a rooted base before calling it a persistent perennial crown. Field scenery cannot prove local identity.
2. In SPCL-b see the actual terminal flowering head partly emerging from an upper sheath. That original three-view plate is an UPPER CULM and sheath, NOT a complete rooted whole plant.

3. Follow the contracted main axis through SPCL-I (green developing short-branch head) and i1 (mature straw tan densely arranged narrow head). It looks spike-like but has lateral branching, so call it a tight PANICLE, not an Elymus-like true spike.

4. In SPCL-I2, J, J1, J2 examine genuine dark exserted ANTHERS on filament-like stalks between green-purple spear-shaped bracts. They are pollen-bearing organs, NOT lemma awns; Sporobolus florets are awnless.

5. One detached sample in SPCL-S shows a real ONE-FLORETED SPIKELET. Locate the two narrow outer GLUMES below one fertile inner lemma/palea. The pale grain shown separately is not an intact spikelet. No new fine arrow until exact glume and palea pixels cross-verified.

6. SPCL-L shows an exact source blade/sheath junction. Real ligule is very SHORT HAIR FRINGE ~0.2–0.3 mm, not a large membranous flap or the broad ragged sheath tissue. Individual hair-tip pinpoint/measurement pending true 20–40× picture.

7. Wet-test study (LINK ONLY, NOT duplicated photograph): on Harms separately documented SPORO comparison the dry S. clandestinus grains vs 20/36-min water microscope shots show PERICARP LOOSENING but still hugging the seed, compared with compositus grains tending to swell/jelly and SLIP. This is not a universal binary test, especially on old/varying collections.

8. True MICROSCOPIC clue (STUDY LINK ONLY): Harms Cscope-lemma research photographed rough-dropseed abundant PRICKLES and silica cells at 100× and 400× versus composite-dropseed larger silica cells and fewer prickle fields and poverty-dropseed hooks. These structures are NOT resolved in any of the new regular phone/photo panels.

9. Compare *S. compositus* actual mature spikelets/seed response and perennial varieties; SPCL narrow spike-like head alone is not diagnostic. Compare *S. vaginiflorus* small seasonal rooted plant and upper-sheath florals; some hidden flowers overlap.

10. Collect and photograph source-identified same living Hays rooted flowering specimen, true glume and lemma at 1mm scale, actual hair ligule microscope and same source mature grain wet test 0/2/5/10/20/40 minutes, and inspect original four source arrows on phone. If missing, hold `FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS`.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: A tight spike-like PANICLE, not a true spike
field_id_short_tiles.details: Find a persistent perennial tuft with an erect 5–10 cm narrowly contracted panicle, sometimes emerging from an inflated upper sheath. The axis has short branches carrying one-flowered spikelets; narrow head shape alone does NOT distinguish rough from composite dropseed. Existing Harms SPCL-I/i1/b show the real inflorescence, not a connected Hays voucher.
field_id_short_tiles.status: GROSS HEAD PHOTOGRAPHED; SAME-VOUCHER ROOT MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · ROOT AND TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Perennial crown; a 0.2–0.3 mm hair fringe
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew GrassBase describes perennial tufted culms about 50–100 cm, narrow blades 1–3 mm, and a TRUE ligule consisting of a 0.2–0.3 mm fringe of hairs on the INNER blade/sheath junction. Do not call the broad sheath mouth a membranous ligule. Existing SPCL-L is a collar-location image, not a resolved 0.2 mm hair-tip measurement.
field_id_short_tiles.status: SOURCE MEASUREMENTS; CALIBRATED INNER LIGULE MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE ONE SPIKELET
field_id_short_tiles.short: 5–7 mm, one fertile floret, no awn
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew describes lanceolate mature spikelets approximately 5–7 mm long, each with ONE fertile floret and no long lemma awn. Purple exserted floral organs in the archived Harms flowering views are ANTHERS, not awns. SPCL-S includes a true detached spikelet and separate grains, but the bracts are not yet individually measured and verified.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · GLUMES AND FERTILE LEMMA
field_id_short_tiles.short: Rough outer glumes, pubescent inner lemma
field_id_short_tiles.details: Kew GrassBase: lower glume about 2–3.5 mm, upper glume 3–4.2 mm; both one-veined, finely asperulous, and shorter than the floret. Fertile lemma approximately 4–5 mm, one-veined, pubescent, and awnless; palea two-veined. A true 1-mm calibrated dissection must separately expose each glume, lemma and palea before adding arrows to those organs.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · GRAIN AND MICROSCOPIC PROOF
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fresh wet pericarp and 400× lemma prickles
field_id_short_tiles.details: Bob Harms's separate SPORO research documents rough-dropseed pericarp loosening on wetting without the strongly gelatinous slipping described for some composite-dropseed material, plus abundant microscopic lemma prickles. These are CONDITIONAL research clues, not proof from the existing public photos; use freshly ripe vouchered grains and a timed wet sequence, then 400× lemma comparison. The research micrographs are study links only, with separate image rights unconfirmed.
field_id_short_tiles.status: RESEARCH LINK ONLY; SAME-VOUCHER WET TEST/400× MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Do not remove a dropseed from panicle silhouette
field_id_short_tiles.details: Composite dropseed (S. compositus) is also perennial and narrow-headed; its variety macer can have true rhizomes, so do not use rhizome absence as a universal split. Poverty dropseed (S. vaginiflorus) is an annual, often with upper-sheath flowering, but concealed flowers occur in relatives. Use rooted growth form, mature glumes/lemma, and expert microscopy for hard separations; when unresolved record Sporobolus sp.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LOOK-ALIKE RULE READY; MATCHED SAME-SCALE PHOTOS MISSING

grass_species_finalization_20261025.scope: Existing canonical rough-dropseed card: six concise crew tiles and exact photo/QA handoffs. No image, arrow, taxonomic status or range change.
NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: One legally documented Hays-region rooted perennial specimen connected to an intact 5–10 cm contracted flowering panicle and centimeter ruler; Harms upper-culm photo does not establish root continuity.
Same-voucher 5–7 mm ripe spikelet with 1-mm scale and separately spread 2–3.5 mm lower glume, 3–4.2 mm upper glume, 4–5 mm pubescent awnless lemma and palea; verify pixels before fine arrows.
True inner collar under 20–40× showing actual 0.2–0.3 mm ligule HAIR fringe with a calibrated 0.5-mm reference; current SPCL-L shows junction but not individually proven hair tips.
Fresh mature grain dry/0/2/5/10/20/40-minute wet comparison on same vouchered specimen and species-authenticated S. compositus; do not generalize from dry grain alone.
Licensed and taxon-vouchered 400× abaxial lemma prickle/silica comparison; Bob Harms SPORO research image rights not cleared for gallery reuse.
NEEDS_SITE_QA: Verify all preexisting photo records and creator/source/license fields, including credited-educational-use Harms Selected Monocots originals; do not extend this permission to separate SPORO microscope images.
Check existing four gross arrows on their actual JPEG pixels and mobile public learner; do not annotate submillimeter hairs, glumes, lemma prickles or wet reactions absent from photographs.
Verify rights-filtered gallery rendering and correctly labelled other-species comparisons separately with Public Learner Readiness; no Pages update claimed.
grass_species_finalization_20261025.public_ready_criteria: Retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until rooted same-voucher specimen, calibrated separated glumes/lemma, real hair ligule, credible fresh-grain/lemma confirmation, per-photo rights, arrows and live QA are independently verified. Never certify from panicle outline.
grass_species_finalization_20261025.preservation: All preexisting image records, photo licenses, annotations, original taxonomy and county status, comparison records and scientific holds preserved.
